sourceInformation.plan: PLAN.md (Game plan: an original surgical-action drama on the Pavilion engine)
sourceInformation.genre: Surgical action (pointer-precision arcade game under a ticking clock) framed by a visual-novel medical melodrama, with drop-in co-op
sourceInformation.perspective: Operations: a fixed surgeon's-eye view looking down at the operative field (73 degrees, mild perspective, short camera pushes); story: a staged paper theatre seen straight on
sourceInformation.tech: Pavilion engine (shardfall repo, commit 49ef2ba) in Rust 1.98.1: wgpu renderer, egui 0.36 shell, winit, gilrs, cpal and a code-written Web Audio synth; wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 to a single HTML file; AI Hub session protocol client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's native cel-shaded style with ink outlines and bloom: a per-frame vertex-painted operative field, SDF instruments and parasites, and layered extruded spline cards for the paper-theatre story
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's sim-driven procedural animation: tool squeeze, cut and recoil, tissue pulse, creeping tendrils, swelling sacs, nodules stepping on the beat, and paper rigs that blink, breathe, sway and flap their mouths
sourceInformation.audio: All in code: about 35 synthesized sound cues, a heartbeat-following note sequencer with ten tracks, and Animalese-style voices (formant blips per syllable); music defaults to 10% volume
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world Code Blue round for 1-4 players (host-authoritative, 15 Hz snapshots and inputs, own pre-op card); the game runs fully on its own outside a session
sourceInformation.testing: Headless only: Rust tests (bot wins on 10 seeds, careless player loses, determinism, coverage, content lint, shell, audio) behind one command; Playwright browser tests on the built file with a stubbed DualSense, keyboard and mouse, phone profile and the AI Hub harness; screenshots only for visuals
sourceInformation.research: Research done by the plan: Trauma Center: Second Opinion (Atlus, Wii launch title, 2006), a remake of the DS Under the Knife; Wii Remote pointer and Nunchuk tool flick, two doctors with different gifts, day-named strains, rank scoring. No further research

testingFeedback: Twelve real defects: a forceps grab that never fired when the trigger was already held, an Echo repeat that invalidated an index and panicked, an unreachable Case 7 nodule (the Scanner slot becomes the Cryoprobe there), a tendril the bot could not pull far enough, an idle player that won Case 7 through the partner bot, a story script under the plan's length, par values that left the bot at rank B, lost menu key taps between slow frames, a test hook that sent the wrong screen command, a Case Files jump that skipped the chart card, hub clients that stayed silent until play began, and a late ready() call.

Five: the covered-hook grab that soft-locked Case 0, the Echo panic, the unreachable Case 7 nodule, the tendril that could not be finished (Case 4 could never be won), and the silent hub clients (the hub's own check fails a game that does not talk both ways).

The headless scripted playthrough of the whole campaign (the bot plays every case and every story scene on ten seeds) plus the coverage counters: they found rule bugs in seconds and proved every tool, hazard, strain, gift and Code fires.
Pixel screenshots of the operative field: useful for the look, but they said little about whether the rules worked, and each cost a build.
engineFeedback: Everything runs headless: the same Sim, bot and capture tools drive tests, balance and screenshots, and the snapshot, rewind and replay hashes made determinism cheap to prove. The single-file web packer worked first time.

Yes. I guessed the egui painter API (0.36 changed run_ui and content_rect), where gilrs keeps analog trigger values, and how the hook's input frame accumulates pressed bits (it only clears its own). The packer silently allows nothing outside the page, so wasm-bindgen snippets are a trap.

A separate product frame path: the engine's App::frame is the Shardfall demo, so the shell, input, camera, audio director and hub bridge for this game live in product.rs, hook.rs and the pav_ui surgery shell.

Memory. The workspace needs several GB per rustc and another agent's build on the same machine got mine killed repeatedly; and the lack of a per-game camera, input and renderer seam, which meant touching frame.rs, input.rs, build.rs, simhost.rs and the app.

Added SimEvent::Cue, SurgeonInput and SurgeryCmd on InputFrame, RenderFrame.surgery, a surgery view early-return in ViewBuilder::build, three audio buses with a band-pass formant filter and a music sequencer in pav_audio, a product frame path in pav_app, a session client, tags and shim in the packer, and the game's own mod under games/surgery.
A real per-game seam: a trait for a game's own frame, camera, input device map and UI, so a game does not fork App::frame.
promptFeedback: The plan: it decided what mattered, marked what had been tested, and named every engine seam up front, so I spent my effort building rather than deciding.

Little was confusing, but the scale was: the plan asks for a whole studio's output (a sim, a view, a theatre, a shell, an audio engine, a hub round, tests and a designer guide) in one sitting, and its own cut list is the only guide to what to drop.

Keeping many large systems consistent: one frame struct feeding the view, the shell, the audio director, the tests and the network mirror, and not breaking the other layers while a single-file build takes minutes on a shared, memory-starved machine.
State the budget (hours or tokens) next to the scope, and give the whole-game vertical slice a ranked must-have list so the least important features can be cut first without guessing.

aiHub.name: Tempo Trauma
aiHub.description: A surgical-action drama in a rain-soaked harbour hospital: eight instruments, a pulse that sets the tempo of everything, and a parasite that keeps time inside the city's patients. Solo, local co-op or an AI Hub Code Blue round.
aiHub.controls: Right stick or mouse aims, R2 or left click operates, left stick flick or 1-8 picks instruments, Triangle or Space fires your gift
